en: Itivuttaka 81:
Tikanipāta, Catutthavagga (The Fourth Chapter)
The Discourse on Honor.
This was said by the Blessed One, said by the Arahant; thus have I heard:

"Bhikkhus, I have seen beings who, overcome by honor, their minds consumed by it, with the breakup of the body, after death, have reappeared in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, a lower realm, even in hell."

“Bhikkhus, I have seen beings who were overwhelmed by lack of honor, their minds consumed by it, and with the breakup of the body, after death, reborn in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, a lower realm, even in hell.

Bhikkhus, I have also seen beings who were overwhelmed by both honor and lack of honor, their minds consumed by them, and with the breakup of the body, after death, reborn in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, a lower realm, even in hell.
And this, bhikkhus, I do not say because I have heard it from another ascetic or brahmin.”
“Furthermore, monks, I speak only of what I have known myself, seen myself, and realized myself.

Monks, I have seen beings overcome by honor, their minds consumed by it, who, with the breakup of the body, after death, have reappeared in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, a lower realm, even in hell.

Monks, I have seen beings overcome by dishonor, their minds consumed by it, who, with the breakup of the body, after death, have reappeared in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, a lower realm, even in hell.”

“Bhikkhus, I have seen beings who, overcome by both honor and dishonor, their minds consumed by them, with the breakup of the body, after death, have been reborn in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, a lower realm, even in hell.
Thus the Blessed One spoke. With reference to this, it is said:
“He for whom both being honored and not being honored do not cause his concentration to waver— ”
Dwelling in heedfulness—
him who meditates constantly,
possessing subtle vision and insight;
"One who delights in the destruction of clinging is called a true person"—
this matter was also spoken by the Blessed One; thus have I heard.
The second.
